identity_reason: a layout primitive only sets inset, ground and corner from closed token sets and has no look of its own to derive
concept: Box is a plain block that sets how far its content stands from the edge, so insets inside a unit are chosen from the module steps and never typed in.

root.why: A box takes no size or position of its own, so its place does not shift between states.

p-none.why: No inset lets a child such as a display window run to the edge of the box.

p-xs.why: The smallest inset is one 4px step, the pitch of the grille holes.

p-sm.why: A two-step inset suits a chip or a label printed close to a part.

p-md.why: A four-step inset keeps printing off the edge and on the inner line of the body.

p-lg.why: The body inset of six steps puts labels on the inset line where case printing sits.

p-xl.why: The section inset of eight steps gives a whole unit room around its face.

s-page.why: The page ground is the plain colour the units stand on, so a box on it adds nothing.

s-raised.why: The raised ground is the body plastic of a unit, the same material height as its neighbours.

s-sunken.why: The sunken ground is a recess in the body, used behind a display or a tray of parts.

c-mark.why: The smallest corner suits a tag or key legend and stays well inside any larger body.

c-media.why: The media corner matches picture and window areas that nest inside the body.

c-inner.why: The inner corner is the outer radius minus the inset, so a box nests in a panel evenly.

c-panel.why: The panel corner is the body radius itself, capped so a large box does not swell into a pillow.
